messages.author: b3aac9b51060928b
messages.subject: MRO 3.2.3 64-bit Crash - Error Unhandled exception at 0x000007FEFEB87D0F (msvcrt.dll) in Rgui.exe
parts:
MRO 3.2.3 64-bit clean install (after uninstalling all previous versions of RRO/R) crashes when typing characters beyond the GUI's current width if the RGui window is made vertically longer.

The error is as follows: 

Unhandled exception at 0x000007FEFEB87D0F (msvcrt.dll) in Rgui.exe: 0xC0000005: Access violation reading location 0x0000000000000000.


My quick search links msvcrt.dll to Visual C++ redistributable.  Does MRO 3.2.3 depend on a particular version of Visual C++ redistributable that isn't packaged with it?


Steps to reproduce:

- OS Win7 Ultimate 64-bit SP1 - 64 GB Ram - Core i7-5930K CPU

- Previously running R 3.2.3 core without issue / Previously running RRO 3.2.0 without issue

- Uninstall all previous versions of RRO/R and manually delete remaining install directories.  Reboot.

- Install MRO 3.2.3 using default installer found here: https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/download/  - with default settings

- Launch MRO 3.2.3

- Increase size of RGui window vertically so that it's slightly larger (or full height, or full screen - Basically, change the vertical height of the window by at least 10%)

- Type commands or characters until they reach the right edge of the RGui window

- MRO will crash and report the above error upon launching debugger


Troubleshooting attempted: 

- Uninstalled and reinstalled multiple times

- Installed latest versions of Visual C++ redistributable (2008, 2010, 2012, 2013, x64)

- Happens even without RevoMath installation 

- Reinstalled base R 3.2.3 -> No issue.  Only occurs with MRO 3.2.3

- Tested with different sizes of RGui window.  Works fine if the default size of the window is left untouched.  Crashes begin after the window is made larger by at least 10%, or full screen, or full height, or similar measures in between.  Horizontal resizing of the window has no effect.  /Shrinking/ the vertical size of the window to smaller than default size has no effect.

- Enabling "Prevent windows from being automatically arranged..." in control panel has no effect

messages.subject: Re: MRO 3.2.3 64-bit Crash - Error Unhandled exception at 0x000007FEFEB87D0F (msvcrt.dll) in Rgui.exe
parts:
Upon further testing, I think I can see what is causing the crash.

In regular R 3.2.3, if you start typing a line and then resize the window, the characters continue typing exactly where you left off.

In MRO 3.2.3, if you start typing a line and then resize the window, the line appears to "copy" as if a carriage return was entered, leaving the previous partial typed amount in the scrollback and continuing on a line further down.  If you play with the resizing, sometimes the lines will "recombine" back into the line in the scrollback and sometimes it will continue character entry below.  It looks really odd.

What's worse is that I've been able to reproduce this issue on RRO 3.2.2, 3.2.1, & 3.2.0 (which I was previously using without issue) and 8.0.3.  That suggests to me that it may be related to a Windows Update patch of some sort since very little else has changed on either of my systems (Win 7 & Win 8.1, both of which reproducing the behaviour consistently).  Have there been any changes in Windows Update related to msvcrt.dll in recent months?  That's my best guess.

messages.author: b3aac9b51060928b
messages.subject: Re: MRO 3.2.3 64-bit Crash - Error Unhandled exception at 0x000007FEFEB87D0F (msvcrt.dll) in Rgui.exe
parts:
Further, this thread seems to suggest that applications need to either distribute their own version of updated msvcrt.dll or compile it into the program directly (making the .exe slightly larger).  Linking directly to the Windows system32 msvcrt.dll is deprecated and Microsoft has stated that it might break due to updates without notice.  My guess is that's what has happened here.

So, is the problem that MRO is liking to the default windows system32 msvcrt.dll and an update has broken it?  If so, it needs to be recompiled with a redistributable version or the redistributable version it is compiled against added to the installer.

See: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1073509/should-i-redistribute-msvcrt-dll-with-my-application & https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/kb/326922 & more recent versions for more recent editions of Visual Studio
